turns.doctor_question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I'm here because... well, I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. It's mainly my hairline and my face. I work as a host at a restaurant, and the lighting there... it just makes me look so old and, I don't know, strange. It's constantly on my mind. My coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, but I just can't shake it. It's really starting to get to me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes being constantly preoccupied with perceived flaws in their hairline and face that coworkers state they do not see.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your appearance in mirrors or other reflective surfaces?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Especially right before a shift. I'll just keep checking the bathroom mirror over and over. I even take pictures on my phone from different angles to see how bad it looks. I'll stand there combing my hair forward, trying to fix it, just... replaying in my head exactly how the guests might see me when I greet them. It gets to the point where I end up running late, or I get so worked up that I can barely bring myself to go out to the front.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive appearance-related behaviors, including repeatedly checking the mirror, taking photos from various angles, and repeatedly combing hair to fix it before shifts.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever avoid work or other social situations because of how you think your appearance looks?
turns.patient_response:
Yes, I do. It's actually gotten me into trouble at work. I’ve been written up at the restaurant because I end up being late, or sometimes I just miss my shifts completely when I can't get past it. 

And outside of work... yeah, I've stopped doing a lot of things. I refuse to be in any staff photos now, and I've stopped going to gallery events and hikes with people. I just... I can’t handle being seen that way.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe there is definitely something wrong with your appearance, even when other people tell you they don’t see it?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. I know they say they don't see it, but... well, I figure they're just being polite, or maybe they just aren't looking as closely as I am. But I know what I see in the mirror. It's definitely there, no matter what anyone else tells me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms a persistent belief that there is a definite flaw in their appearance despite others stating they cannot see it.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from your appearance, do you also get unwanted thoughts that keep bothering you about other things?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It's... it's just my appearance. I don't really have unwanted thoughts about anything else, just the way I look. That's the only thing that gets stuck in my head like that.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms that persistent thoughts about their appearance and the way they look get stuck in their head.
symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly denies having unwanted, intrusive thoughts about other subjects beyond their appearance.

turns.doctor_question: Is there any chance you might be mistaken about how abnormal your hairline or face looks?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't think I'm mistaken. I mean, I look in the mirror every day, and it's right there. I know what I see. It's not something I'm just imagining. My hairline is receding in this really uneven way, and my face just... it looks wrong. I know people say it's fine, but they aren't the ones who have to live with it. I'm absolutely certain about how bad it looks.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient firmly insists their hairline and face look wrong and defective despite other people assuring them that it is fine, confirming preoccupation with perceived appearance flaws.
